summary: Elisabeth Schüssler Fiorenza is a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Würzburg and the University of Münster. She held posts at the University of Notre Dame (1970–1984), Episcopal Divinity School (1984–1988), and Harvard University (1988).

Eliz Hale works in religious and Buddhist studies. Hale earned a B.S. at the University of Mississippi (2018–2022), a Ph.D. at UC Davis (2023), and is attested as a graduate student at UC Santa Barbara in 2026.

Eliza Marian Butler studied at Newnham College, Cambridge (~1909–1913). She held posts at the University of Manchester (1936), Owens College (~1936–1945), and the University of Cambridge (~1945–1951).

Elizabeth A. Cecil is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and archaeology. She completed her PhD at Brown University under James L. Fitzgerald and held posts at the University of Groningen, Leiden University, and Florida State University.

Elizabeth Colton Spooner was an Indology scholar who studied at the American Institute of Sacred Literature, Yale University, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University, where she was taught by Charles Rockwell Lanman.

Elizabeth De Michelis is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at SOAS and earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge (~1996–2001), where she served as director in 2000 before working at the University of Oxford.

Elizabeth English is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Oxford by 1999, studying under doctoral supervisor Alexis Sanderson and teacher Harunaga Isaacson.

Elizabeth Errington is a historian, archaeologist, and Indologist. She studied at SOAS under Adrian David Hugh Bivar and held posts at the British Museum from 1993, the Fitzwilliam Museum (1992), and the University of Oxford (~2016).

Elizabeth Guthrie is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Canterbury by 1994 and served as a tutor in Religious Studies at the University of Otago, attested in 2007.

Elizabeth J. Harris works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her doctorate under Ananda Guruge and Yakupitiyage Karunadasa at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and University of Kelaniya, holding posts at Westminster College and University of Birmingham.

Elizabeth J. Perry is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Michigan (~1971–1978) and held academic posts at the University of Washington (~1978–1990) and Harvard University (~1997).

Elizabeth Morrison is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned her Ph.D. at Stanford University under Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt. She held posts at Amherst College (1998–1999) and Middlebury College (2003).

Elizabeth Napper is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at the University of Virginia under Paul Groner and Jeffrey Hopkins. She served as co-director of the Tibetan Nuns Project, attested 2001–2006.
Elizabeth Stuart is a religious studies scholar who founded Theology & Sexuality and served as a director at the University of Winchester in 2021.
Elke Rogersdotter is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who completed a PhD attested in 2006 at Umeå University under Thomas B. Larsson, Bozena Werbart, Karin Viklund, and P. Ajithprasad.

Ellen M. Raven is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who has held posts at Leiden University (attested 2003 and 2018) and served on the editorial board of Gonda Indological Studies (attested 2018).

Elliot M. Stern is an Indology scholar who studied under P. N. Pattabhirama Sastri (1978–1979) and earned doctoral degrees at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona and Wilhelm Halbfass (attested 1988).

Elliot Sperling was a Tibetologist and historian who earned his degrees at Queens College, CUNY, and Indiana University Bloomington. He served as associate professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1987–2015) and held posts at Harvard and the University of Delhi.

Ellison Banks Findly is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies who studied under Fred Pfeil. She held posts at Mount Holyoke College and Trinity College, Hartford, where she was an associate professor attested in 1989.

Ellwood Austin Welden was an Indologist and linguist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Pennsylvania (~1903–1906). He held positions at the University of Maine, Bryn Mawr College, the Lawrenceville School, and the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce.
